answer: Practically, the chain should fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because anchor only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, horizon is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any lantern approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
